## Step 1: Understanding the Write-Ahead Log
A write-ahead log is a mechanism used by databases to ensure data integrity and facilitate recovery after a crash. It's essentially a log of all operations - inserts, updates, and deletes - before they are applied to the database. This log is written to a separate area of the disk, independent of the database files.

## Step 2: The Role of the Write-Ahead Log in Recovery
When a database system experiences a crash, the data in memory may not be persisted to the actual database files. However, the write-ahead log captures all operations in a sequence, including any partially completed transactions. This log serves as a record of all intended changes that were not yet committed to the database.
